attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his view.

semantics.note: Keeps both categorical parts: no novel concepts, and inconsistent and unreliable. Leaves out the 'vary wildly' clause, a minor omission. It is a present-tense capability claim, so observation fits.

contract.note: Reading 'novel concepts' as useful new ideas or methods is an ordinary reading, though he may have meant fundamental breakthroughs. Counting LLM-plus-search systems is also a choice of interpretation. The 2025 window is chosen by the evaluator but reasonable.

evidence.note: 2025 tau2-bench preprint. Repeated trials show substantial failures and falling pass^k, which supports the unreliability part for the tasks tested.
DeepMind's own disclosure of a new 11-dimension kissing bound (593) and a new 4x4 matrix algorithm. Under the contract, a developer claim needs corroboration, which e3 gives.
Aalto University account, external to DeepMind, treats AlphaEvolve's 593 bound as the current record in dimension 11. That corroborates a genuinely new result, though it is not a replication.
GUI-testing study finds some LLMs effective with guardrails. This limits a blanket unreliability reading but does not settle it.

reviews.rationale: Mixed. The reliability part holds: e1 shows substantial repeated-task failures in 2025. The categorical novelty denial fails under the contract's plain reading: AlphaEvolve produced a new kissing-number bound, reported by DeepMind and recognised by Aalto University. That result depends on counting a new construction as a 'novel concept' and on including LLM-plus-search systems, which the contract does.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Correctly states the comparative causal claim (credit availability matters more than compute demand). Rightly drops the 'every investor' framing as rhetoric.

contract.note: He gave no measure of relative causal weight. Requiring evidence that separates credit effects from demand effects is a fair, ordinary standard. The fiscal-2026 period is inferred from the surrounding text.

evidence.note: CoreWeave disclosure of a bank loan facility for equipment tied to OpenAI. It shows debt-financed buying but does not separate causal effects.
NVIDIA's Q3 FY26 release says demand is strong. As a company disclosure, it does not establish causal weight relative to financing.

reviews.rationale: Unresolved. Nothing in the packet separates the effect of credit supply from end-user demand on NVIDIA sales. e1 shows that debt financing exists. e2 is management's own claim about demand. Neither meets the contract's causal-evidence requirement.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement in his post.

semantics.note: An unqualified 'will make no more than $5B this year', written 29 Dec 2025. A firm forecast about 2025 revenue. Rightly leaves out the funding figures.

contract.note: Reading 'make' as realised 2025 revenue is ordinary. The contract makes scoring depend on establishing which accounting basis he meant, which he never supplied. That leaves open whether gross or net treatment could cross $5B.

evidence.note: WIRED, 26 Oct 2026 (before the evaluation date), summarises the S-1: about $4.5B 2025 revenue, GAAP $4.585B. Below the ceiling, but its basis is not matched to the claim's unknown basis.

reviews.rationale: Unresolved. The horizon (end of 2025) has passed. Reported GAAP 2025 revenue (~$4.585B) is under $5B, which leans toward support. But the contract requires the claim's accounting basis to be established, and it is not, so per policy the different-basis figure is context only.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast in his post.

semantics.note: Wording is preserved. Grammatically, only the panic sentence depends on a startup dying; the first two sentences could be read as unconditional, and the contract notes this. Horizon 'for a while' is open.

contract.note: Treating the whole passage as conditional, the 50% baseline, and the meaning of 'death' are all evaluator interpretations. They are reasonable, and the contract flags them.

evidence.note: Character.AI Chapter 11 sale process, Oct 2026. It is not a named referent, and a sale is not yet a death. Says nothing on VC holding values or panic.

reviews.rationale: Unresolved. The antecedent (a qualifying startup death) is not established: Character.AI is in a sale process and is not clearly a referent. There is no deadline and no conclusive event, and no evidence covers holding values, VC fundraising, or an acquisition panic.
